definitions.explanation: Describes something that is completely covered or smeared with mud.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもが{泥|どろ}だらけで{帰|かえ}ってきた。
examples.english: The child came home covered in mud.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}の{後|あと}、{靴|くつ}が{泥|どろ}だらけになった。
examples.english: My shoes got muddy after the rain.

examples.japanese: {泥|どろ}だらけの{手|て}で{触|さわ}らないで。
examples.english: Don't touch things with your muddy hands.

notes:
USAGE:
{泥|どろ}だらけ uses the suffix ～だらけ, which means "covered in" or "full of" (usually something unpleasant). It functions as a の-adjective modifying nouns ({泥|どろ}だらけの{服|ふく}) or with the copula ({泥|どろ}だらけだ).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {泥|どろ}だらけの{服|ふく} (mud-covered clothes)
- {泥|どろ}だらけになる (to get covered in mud)
- {泥|どろ}だらけの{道|みち} (muddy road)

PATTERN:
The ～だらけ suffix attaches to nouns to mean "covered with" or "full of": {傷|きず}だらけ (covered in scratches), {血|ち}だらけ (covered in blood), {間違|まちが}いだらけ (full of mistakes). It almost always has a negative or unpleasant connotation.
